Official technical description / test: Intended purpose or reasonably foreseeable use includes direct or indirect logical/physical data connection to a device or network; product includes hardware/software and separately marketed components.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: Likely in scope if the drive's intended/foreseeable use includes fieldbus/Ethernet/controller data connection; exact SKU and market configuration evidence required.
Separately marketed component assessment: A separately marketed software/hardware component may itself be a product with digital elements.
Evidence required: Exact SKU, intended purpose, connection diagrams, product brochure/manual, EU market placing date, separate component sales boundary.
Conformity route: CRA scope gate before category assessment.

CRA legal basis: Article 7(1); Annex III; Reg. 2025/2392 Annex I Class I point 10
Official technical description / test: Physical interface directly connects a device to a network via driver API, typically data-link layer, with hardware adapter and firmware; includes controllers/adapters for Ethernet and Fieldbus. Virtual interface connects via API emulating physical interface drivers.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: Whole servo drive's core function is motion control, not network interfacing; built-in fieldbus port alone does not conclusively make the whole drive a network-interface product. Keep Unknown until core-function and product-boundary evidence.
Separately marketed component assessment: A separately sold Fieldbus/Ethernet interface card, controller or adapter may meet the category definition.
Evidence required: Whether interface board is separately placed on market; driver/API, protocol stack, hardware adapter, firmware, product datasheet, intended purpose.
Conformity route: If classified Class I: Article 32(2) logic; Module A only where all applicable HEN/CS/EUCC at substantial assurance are applied; otherwise B+C or H.

CRA legal basis: Article 7(1); Annex III; Reg. 2025/2392 Annex I Class I point 14
Official technical description / test: MCU provides encryption, authentication, secure key storage, RNG, TEE or hardware protections aimed to secure other products, networks or services beyond the MCU itself.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: No product-level classification from MCU presence alone; determine whether the drive itself has the category's core functionality.
Separately marketed component assessment: A separately marketed security MCU may qualify if exact technical definition is met; integrated MCU does not automatically reclassify the drive.
Evidence required: Exact MCU part number, datasheet/security manual, security features, intended security purpose, whether component sold separately.
Conformity route: If MCU itself is Class I product, apply Article 32(2) to that component product; host drive assessed separately.

CRA legal basis: Article 7(1); Annex III; Reg. 2025/2392 Annex I Class I point 13/15
Official technical description / test: Integrated circuits with security functions such as encryption, authentication, key storage, RNG, TEE or hardware protection aimed to secure other products/services.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: No evidence that servo drive's core functionality is such an IC product.
Separately marketed component assessment: Separately marketed chip may be Class I if it meets the technical description.
Evidence required: BOM, exact chip IDs, security capabilities, vendor manuals, product sales boundary.
Conformity route: Article 32(2) if the separately marketed component is Class I.

CRA legal basis: Article 7(1); Annex III; Reg. 2025/2392 Annex I Class I point 11
Official technical description / test: Software provides an abstract interface to underlying hardware and controls execution of software, including real-time and special-purpose OS.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: Embedded RTOS/firmware inside a servo drive does not automatically make the complete drive an OS product; core function remains product-specific.
Separately marketed component assessment: Separately marketed OS/RTOS may be a product with core functionality of an OS.
Evidence required: OS name/version, license/supply model, whether marketed separately, system architecture and core functionality.
Conformity route: Article 32(2) if OS product is Class I.

CRA legal basis: Article 7(1); Annex III; Reg. 2025/2392 Annex I Class I point 5
Official technical description / test: Establishes encrypted logical tunnel constructed from physical or virtual network resources.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: No evidence of VPN core function in servo drive; remote access alone is insufficient. ETSI EN 304 620 excludes industrial OT VPN systems from its scope.
Separately marketed component assessment: A separately marketed VPN gateway/client/server must be assessed as its own product.
Evidence required: VPN tunnel architecture, crypto endpoint role, marketed product boundary, intended OT/IT use.
Conformity route: Article 32(2) if VPN product is Class I.

CRA legal basis: Article 7(1); Annex III; Reg. 2025/2392 Annex I Class I point 6
Official technical description / test: Manages connected network elements by monitoring them and controlling network operations/configuration; includes end-to-end and dedicated configuration management systems.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: Drive commissioning/configuration tool limited to drive parameters is not automatically an NMS; product's managed network elements and core function must be assessed. ETSI EN 304 621 excludes industrial OT NMS.
Separately marketed component assessment: Separately marketed NMS platform may be Class I.
Evidence required: List of managed network elements, monitoring/control functions, network scope, product marketing, user documentation.
Conformity route: Article 32(2) if NMS product is Class I.

CRA legal basis: Article 7(1); Annex III; Reg. 2025/2392 Annex I Class I point 7
Official technical description / test: Collects data from multiple sources, analyses/correlates it and presents actionable information for security purposes.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: Drive alarm/event log alone is not a SIEM. ETSI EN 304 622 excludes industrial OT SIEM systems.
Separately marketed component assessment: Separately marketed SIEM platform may be Class I.
Evidence required: Multi-source data ingestion, correlation/analytics, security use purpose, product boundary.
Conformity route: Article 32(2) if SIEM product is Class I.

CRA legal basis: Article 7(1); Annex III; Reg. 2025/2392 Annex I Class I point 12
Official technical description / test: Routers route traffic between networks; modems convert analogue/digital signals for IP communications; switches forward packets and have a management plane.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: An Ethernet/EtherCAT port does not make a servo drive a router, modem or switch.
Separately marketed component assessment: Separately marketed network appliance may be Class I.
Evidence required: Routing protocols, packet forwarding, management plane, modem function, product brochure and SKU boundary.
Conformity route: Article 32(2) if network appliance is Class I.

CRA legal basis: Article 7(1); Annex III; Reg. 2025/2392 Annex I Class II point 2
Official technical description / test: Firewall protects connected network/system by monitoring and restricting traffic; IDS monitors traffic for suspicious activity; IPS actively responds.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: Integrated filtering/diagnostic feature does not automatically make servo drive a Class II security appliance; core functionality test required.
Separately marketed component assessment: A separately marketed firewall/IDS/IPS appliance may be Class II.
Evidence required: Traffic inspection/enforcement architecture, standalone product purpose, datasheet, intended use, separate SKU.
Conformity route: Article 32(3): B+C, H, or available/applicable EUCC at least substantial.

CRA legal basis: Article 8(1); Annex IV; Reg. 2025/2392 Annex II point 1
Official technical description / test: Securely stores/processes/manages sensitive data or performs cryptographic operations; multiple discrete components; physical envelope provides tamper evidence/resistance/response.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: Ordinary servo drive enclosure is insufficient. No evidence that drive's core function is a tamper-protected cryptographic hardware device.
Separately marketed component assessment: A separately marketed HSM/security box may meet the category.
Evidence required: Tamper evidence/resistance/response design, enclosure construction, crypto/data purpose, multi-component architecture, security certification.
Conformity route: Article 32(4): EUCC if required under Article 8(1) delegated act; otherwise Article 32(3) routes.

CRA legal basis: Article 8(1); Annex IV; Reg. 2025/2392 Annex II point 2
Annex/category: Smart meter gateways / advanced secure cryptoprocessing devices
Official technical description / test: Controls communications in smart metering systems and authorised third parties; protects metering/data flows, supports cryptography, may include firewalling and device control.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: No evidence a servo drive is a smart meter gateway or equivalent advanced security device.
Separately marketed component assessment: Separately marketed smart meter gateway/security appliance must be assessed.
Evidence required: Intended smart-meter role, utility integration, authorised third-party communication, cryptoprocessing, product boundary.

CRA legal basis: Article 8(1); Annex IV; Reg. 2025/2392 Annex II point 3
Annex/category: Smartcards or similar devices, including secure elements
Official technical description / test: Secure element with security functions and tamper evidence/resistance/response, cryptographic or sensitive data handling, at least AVA_VAN.4; may be discrete or integrated in SoC.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: Integrated secure element does not automatically make complete drive a critical product; assess complete product core function and any separately marketed secure component.
Separately marketed component assessment: A separately marketed TPM/secure element may meet category if technical assurance criteria are met.
Evidence required: Exact secure element/TPM part, Common Criteria AVA_VAN.4 evidence, tamper features, whether separately placed on market.

Official technical description / test: Manufacturer may use Module A, B+C, H, or where available/applicable an EU cybersecurity certification scheme.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: Applicable only after proving the complete product is not Annex III/IV core-function category.
Separately marketed component assessment: Separate components may have their own route.
Evidence required: Final product classification and Annex I risk assessment.
Conformity route: Module A or B+C or H or applicable EUCC.

Official technical description / test: If applicable HEN/CS/EUCC at substantial assurance is not applied or only partly applied, or none exists, submit to B+C or H; full application permits Article 32(1) route.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: Do not select route until core functionality and actual applicable HEN/OJ/CS/EUCC state are proven.
Separately marketed component assessment: Class I component product follows its own route.
Evidence required: Actual OJ-cited HEN scope, CS/EUCC assurance, evidence of full application.
Conformity route: Module A only when full relevant standard/specification/certification application condition is met; otherwise B+C or H.

Official technical description / test: B+C, H, or where available/applicable EUCC at least substantial.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: Only if complete product's core functionality is Class II.
Separately marketed component assessment: Separate Class II security appliance follows its own route.
Evidence required: Class II core-functionality evidence and available EUCC scheme.
Conformity route: B+C or H or EUCC substantial.

Official technical description / test: EUCC where Article 8(1) delegated act requires it; if conditions are not met/no such delegated act, Article 32(3) route.
Servo-drive complete-product assessment: No Annex IV classification evidence for a conventional servo drive at this stage.
Separately marketed component assessment: A separately marketed security box/secure element may need independent review.
Evidence required: Check current Article 8 delegated acts and Annex IV technical description.
